name: I-Wak
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only comparative/overview refs (Himes 1998 Southern Cordilleran, Zorc 1986); no descriptive grammar or phonology of I-Wak.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1979. On the development of contrastive word accent: Pangasinan, a case in point. In Nguyen Dang Liem (ed.), South-East Asian Linguistic Studies 3, 241-258. Pacific Linguistics C-45

sources.note: Pangasinan accent; cites Inibaloi, Kallahan (Kayapa), Ilongot forms; no I-Wak mention.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1978. Proto-Philippine word accent: innovation or Proto-Hesperonesian retention? Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings, 67-119. Pacific Linguistics C-61
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative accent study; no I-Wak data or mention.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid iwak1237 (web page and JSON) and Glottolog hh.bib (local copy)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Repository and database searches: ScholarSpace (UH) for 'Iwak', 'I-wak', 'Iwaak', 'Southern Cordilleran'; ANU Open Research; Crossref; archive.org; lexibank ABVD and ACD language lists
sources.note: No I-Wak-specific item anywhere; ABVD and ACD contain no Iwak doculect.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'I-wak' (Internet Archive copy 2016-03-04)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Alternate name Iwaak; 3,260 speakers (2000); Itogon (Benguet) and Kayapa (Nueva Vizcaya); 'Dialects: None known. Related to Karao, Ibaloi, and Kalanguya'; no language resources listed; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Ruffolo, Paula. 2004. Topics in the morpho-syntax of Ibaloy, Northern Philippines. PhD thesis, Australian National University. Sec. 1.2 Stress, p. 12 fn. 1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Ibaloy, not I-Wak: 'Root stress in Ibaloy is predictable.. The predictability of root stress is a Nuclear Southern Cordilleran (NuSC) feature (Himes, 1998) that Ibaloy retains.' Figure 2 (Himes 1998:121) shows NuSC = Ibaloy, Kalanguya, Karaw. I-Wak is not mentioned anywhere in the thesis.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Terms for rice agriculture and terrace building in some Cordilleran languages of the Philippines. In Pawley & Ross (eds), Austronesian terminologies, 363-388. Pacific Linguistics C-127
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Names 'I'wak' once in the list of Southern Cordilleran languages (Ilongot, Inibaloi, I'wak, Karaw, Kallahan); no I'wak data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1986. The genetic relationships of Philippine languages. In Geraghty, Carrington & Wurm (eds), FOCAL II, 147-173. Pacific Linguistics C-94 (Glottolog ref 10141)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Subgrouping paper; no mention of I-Wak/Iwak in the text and no stress statement for any Southern Cordilleran language.
No phonology or stress information; references are Ethnologue, Glottolog, Himes 1998, Reid 2006, Zorc 1979.

sources.citation: Santiago, Paul Julian. 2010. The Phonetic Structures of Kalanguya. Thesis, University of the Philippines (as named in this project's earlier scan note for ahin1234; record not verified by me)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Closest described relative (Kalanguya, same Nuclear Southern Cordilleran node; Ethnologue notes the Nueva Vizcaya I-wak may speak only Kalanguya). Would give the nearest first-hand stress description, not an I-Wak statement.

sources.citation: Himes, Ronald S. 1998. The Southern Cordilleran Group of Philippine Languages. Oceanic Linguistics 37(1): 120-177.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Comparative-historical study and the only published work carrying I-Wak data (Himes's own fieldwork; hh.bib language code lists I-Wak). Ruffolo 2004 cites it for the claim that predictable root stress is a Nuclear Southern Cordilleran feature; it very likely gives a phoneme/accent statement per language, including I-Wak, and its subgrouping puts I-Wak with Ibaloy.
